column6: quote
Encourage farming and silk: the root of food and clothing.
Take the axe to the hills in season, and timber will never run short.
The Treatise on Architecture: like things grouped, every rule set down.
Steel stirred and forged a hundred times, hard yet supple.
Coins cast to circulate, weighing all the goods under heaven.
When the Zhengguo Canal was done, the land within the passes became fertile and knew no famine.
When the granaries are full, the people know propriety.
Measure what comes in, then decide what goes out.
The realm divided into prefectures, each with its governor, commandant and inspector.
A craftsman who would do good work must first sharpen his tools.
Orders sent by relay stations travel faster than any rider.
Tilling while standing guard, the army has both soldiers and grain.
Move the people to fill the frontier, and walled towns rise on empty land.
Who excels at learning may serve the state.
A farmer's son at dawn, in the emperor's hall by dusk.
A million piculs of grain shipped up the canals each year to fill the capital.
Iron coins weighed too much in Shu, so the people wrote notes and called them jiaozi.
Households in tens vouch for each other: soldiers when called, farmers when home.
The Compendium of Materia Medica: every school gathered, the nature of each thing examined.
The realm divided into ten circuits, following its mountains and rivers.
The Exploitation of the Works of Nature: prize the five grains above gold and jade.
Granaries full, the people prosperous, all under heaven at peace.
Branch secretariats set up in every province, to govern the far lands as the near.
Estates of the crown in every province, their harvests sent to the capital.
Know the enemy and know yourself: a hundred battles without peril.
Soldiers bound into companies, every camp with its rules.
The crossbow is the great strength of the Middle Kingdom.
War is the great affair of the state, and in war the horse is the greatest asset.
With strong armour and sharp blades, the soldiers stand firm.
The eight formations complete, the regular and the surprise give birth to each other.
Deep moats, high ramparts, walls held and fields cleared.
The divine arm bow shoots three hundred paces and pierces heavy armour.
Infantry armour of fifty catties, which neither blade nor arrow can enter.
Galloping and hunting, drawing the bow at full stretch.
Before the troops move, the grain and fodder go first.
Hunts in every season, to teach the ways of war.
Officers chosen by bow and horse, ranked by essays on strategy.
Send scouts far ahead, and keep the beacon towers watchful.
Saltpetre, sulphur and charcoal, mixed together into the fire drug.
Feed on the enemy's grain, and the army will never go hungry.
Wound powders and salves, healing the hurt among the camps.
Long weapons and short ones helping each other, shields and brushes guarding all.
Firearms learnt in the southern campaign, and a battalion raised to drill with them.
The iron horsemen burst forth with a clash of blades and spears.
The day the royal army recovers the central plains.
Commissioners hold the frontier commands, each with his own army and supplies.
